title: "Nonnormality"

If all the eigenvalues of a matrix are negative, then every solution of the
linear ODE system $u'(t) = Au(t)$ eventually decays to zero.  Does that mean the
solution shrinks from the start?

## A diagonal system

Consider the simple system of ODEs:

$$
u_1'(t) = -u_1(t), \qquad u_2'(t) = -10\, u_2(t) .
$$

Each component decays exponentially on its own: $u_1(t)$ like $e^{-t}$ and $u_2(t)$
like $e^{-10t}$.  Here we visualize the components of $u(t)$ (left) and the
length $\|u(t)\|$ (right) over time.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof t1 = timeSlider()
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
figure(solve([1, 0], [0, 1], 60), t1)
```

In the left plot, the blue and green arrows are the two components of $u(t)$,
and the dashed lines show the directions they point in.  Both arrows shrink:
the green one quickly and the blue one slowly.  Since both components shrink,
so does the length $\|u(t)\|$ of the vector $u(t) = (u_1(t), u_2(t))$.

In matrix form, this system is

$$
u'(t) = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -10 \end{bmatrix} u(t) .
$$

The eigenvalues are the diagonal entries, $-1$ and $-10$, and the
eigenvectors point along the two axes (the dashed lines in the plot above).

**If $\boldsymbol{A}$ is a matrix with negative eigenvalues, the solution of**

$$
\boldsymbol{u'(t) = A u(t)}
$$

**must always decay to zero eventually.  But does it always decay monotonically?**

## A coupled system with perpendicular eigenvectors

To answer this question, next consider

$$
u'(t) = \begin{bmatrix} -5.5 & 4.5 \\ 4.5 & -5.5 \end{bmatrix} u(t) .
$$

The two equations are coupled.  But the matrix has the same eigenvalues, $-1$
and $-10$, so each eigencomponent must decay.  The solution is visualized
below, with the eigenvectors again indicated in green and blue.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof t2 = timeSlider()
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
figure(solve([Math.SQRT1_2, Math.SQRT1_2], [-Math.SQRT1_2, Math.SQRT1_2], 60), t2)
```

The eigenvectors are rotated by $45^\circ$, but otherwise nothing has changed:
the two arrows shrink and stay perpendicular, so the length of $u(t)$ shrinks
too.  Notice that the
component $u_1(t)$ grows at first (from 0.5 to about 0.55).  Nevertheless, the
length of the overall vector is monotonically decreasing.

## A system with non-perpendicular eigenvectors

Finally, consider the system

$$
u'(t) = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 30 \\ 0 & -10 \end{bmatrix} u(t) .
$$

The matrix is triangular, so its eigenvalues are still the diagonal entries,
$-1$ and $-10$.  But its eigenvectors are no longer perpendicular.  One still
points along the horizontal axis, while the other is nearly parallel to it.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof t3 = timeSlider()
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
figure(triangular(30, 60), t3)
```

As before, each component is shrinking over time, but now the overall solution
more than doubles in length before it decays!

A matrix whose eigenvectors are perpendicular is called *normal*.  The first two
examples are normal; the third is not.  If a normal matrix has negative
eigenvalues, the length of the solution always decreases monotonically.  But
with a non-normal matrix, the solution can grow dramatically before eventually
decaying.

The same mechanism lies behind the transient growth of powers of non-normal
matrices, which matters in the stability analysis of numerical methods, and
behind transient amplification in fluid flows whose linearizations have only
decaying modes.  A good reference is the book *Spectra and Pseudospectra* by
Trefethen and Embree.

This page is based on a
[Jupyter notebook](https://github.com/ketch/ODE-counterexamples/blob/master/Vinograd-Dekker-Verwer.ipynb)
that goes on to a more surprising example, due to Vinograd: if the matrix
changes in time, the solution can grow without bound even though the
eigenvalues stay fixed and negative.

## Experiment

Here you can also change the upper-right entry $a_{12}$ of the last matrix and
the direction of the initial vector.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof corner = Inputs.range([0, 60], {value: 30, step: 1, label: tex`a_{12}`})
viewof psi4 = Inputs.range([0, 180], {value: 60, step: 1, label: "initial direction"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
tex.block`u'(t) = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & ${corner} \\ 0 & -10 \end{bmatrix} u(t)`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof t4 = timeSlider()
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
figure(triangular(corner, psi4), t4)
```

Things to try:

- Make $a_{12}$ larger.  The eigenvectors become more nearly
  parallel and the growth becomes larger.
- Make it smaller.  At zero you have the diagonal system again.  Below about
  6, the solution doesn't grow from any starting direction, even though the
  eigenvectors aren't perpendicular.
- Start along one of the eigenvectors.  The solution doesn't grow.  Starting
  close to one gives very little growth.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
tMax = 3  // final time shown
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Exact solution of u'(t) = A u(t) with u(0) = (cos psi, sin psi), where A has
// eigenvalues -1 and -10 with unit eigenvectors r1 and r2:
// u(t) = z1 e^{-t} r1 + z2 e^{-10t} r2.
function solve(r1, r2, psiDeg) {
  const l1 = -1, l2 = -10;
  const psi = psiDeg * Math.PI / 180, u0 = [Math.cos(psi), Math.sin(psi)];
  // Solve [r1 r2] z = u0.
  const det = r1[0] * r2[1] - r2[0] * r1[1];
  const z1 = (u0[0] * r2[1] - r2[0] * u0[1]) / det;
  const z2 = (r1[0] * u0[1] - u0[0] * r1[1]) / det;
  const parts = t => {
    const c1 = z1 * Math.exp(l1 * t), c2 = z2 * Math.exp(l2 * t);
    const p1 = [c1 * r1[0], c1 * r1[1]];
    return {p1, u: [p1[0] + c2 * r2[0], p1[1] + c2 * r2[1]]};
  };
  const path = d3.range(0, tMax + 1e-9, 0.005).map(t => {
    const {u} = parts(t);
    return {t, x: u[0], y: u[1], norm: Math.hypot(u[0], u[1])};
  });
  const L = 1.1 * Math.max(1, Math.abs(z1), Math.abs(z2), d3.max(path, d => Math.max(Math.abs(d.x), Math.abs(d.y))));
  return {r1, r2, u0, parts, path, L};
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Solution for the triangular matrix [[-1, b], [0, -10]], whose eigenvectors
// are (1, 0) and the direction of (-b, 9).
function triangular(b, psiDeg) {
  const n = Math.hypot(b, 9);
  return solve([1, 0], [-b / n, 9 / n], psiDeg);
}

// The time slider; changing the other controls doesn't reset it.
function timeSlider() {
  const input = Inputs.range([0, tMax], {value: 0, step: tMax / 300, label: tex`t`});
  input.style.setProperty("--label-width", "1.5rem");  // keep the short label next to its slider
  return input;
}

// At most 5 tick values for an axis running from lo to hi.
function fewTicks(lo, hi) {
  for (let n = 5; n > 0; n--) {
    const ticks = d3.ticks(lo, hi, n);
    if (ticks.length <= 5) return ticks;
  }
  return [];
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Phase plane and length plot for the solution from solve(), at time tNow.
function figure(sys, tNow) {
  const {r1, r2, L, path, parts, u0} = sys;
  const {p1, u} = parts(tNow);
  const blue = "#1f77b4", green = "#2ca02c";
  // The plots are drawn at this size and scaled by CSS to share the column:
  // side by side when it is wide enough, stacked on narrow screens.
  const size = 310;
  const circle = d3.range(0, 2 * Math.PI + 0.01, 0.02).map(s => [Math.cos(s), Math.sin(s)]);
  const phase = Plot.plot({
    width: size, height: size, marginLeft: 40, marginBottom: 30,
    x: {domain: [-L, L], label: null, ticks: fewTicks(-L, L), tickFormat: "~g"},
    y: {domain: [-L, L], label: null, ticks: fewTicks(-L, L), tickFormat: "~g"},
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleX([0], {strokeOpacity: 0.2}), Plot.ruleY([0], {strokeOpacity: 0.2}),
      // eigenvector directions
      Plot.line([[-L * r1[0], -L * r1[1]], [L * r1[0], L * r1[1]]], {stroke: blue, strokeOpacity: 0.5, strokeDasharray: "4,4"}),
      Plot.line([[-L * r2[0], -L * r2[1]], [L * r2[0], L * r2[1]]], {stroke: green, strokeOpacity: 0.5, strokeDasharray: "4,4"}),
      Plot.line(circle, {strokeOpacity: 0.3}),
      Plot.line(path, {x: "x", y: "y", strokeOpacity: 0.5}),
      Plot.arrow([{x1: 0, y1: 0, x2: p1[0], y2: p1[1]}], {x1: "x1", y1: "y1", x2: "x2", y2: "y2", stroke: blue, strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.arrow([{x1: p1[0], y1: p1[1], x2: u[0], y2: u[1]}], {x1: "x1", y1: "y1", x2: "x2", y2: "y2", stroke: green, strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.dot([u0], {x: d => d[0], y: d => d[1], r: 4, stroke: "currentColor"}),
      Plot.dot([u], {x: d => d[0], y: d => d[1], r: 5, fill: "currentColor"})
    ]
  });
  // Axis labels inside the phase plane, at the right end of the horizontal axis
  // and the top of the vertical one; positions in percent so they follow CSS scaling.
  const pct = (x, y) => [100 * phase.scale("x").apply(x) / size, 100 * phase.scale("y").apply(y) / size];
  const [x1, y1] = pct(L, 0), [x2, y2] = pct(0, L);
  const axisLabel = (x, y, shift, label) => html`<div style="position: absolute; left: ${x}%; top: ${y}%;
    transform: ${shift}; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1">${label}</div>`;
  const phaseLabels = [
    axisLabel(x1, y1, "translate(-100%, -120%)", tex`u_1`),
    axisLabel(x2, y2, "translate(.4rem, 0)", tex`u_2`)
  ];
  const ymax = 1.05 * Math.max(1, d3.max(path, d => d.norm));
  const norms = Plot.plot({
    width: size, height: size, marginLeft: 40, marginBottom: 50,
    x: {domain: [0, tMax], label: null, ticks: fewTicks(0, tMax), tickFormat: "~g"},
    y: {domain: [0, ymax], label: null, grid: true, ticks: fewTicks(0, ymax), tickFormat: "~g"},
    marks: [
      Plot.line(path, {x: "t", y: "norm", strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.ruleX([tNow], {strokeOpacity: 0.3}),
      Plot.dot([{t: tNow, n: Math.hypot(u[0], u[1])}], {x: "t", y: "n", r: 5, fill: "currentColor"})
    ]
  });
  for (const p of [phase, norms]) Object.assign(p.style, {width: "100%", height: "auto"});
  // y-axis label as a box in the empty upper-right corner (the curves decay toward the bottom)
  const yLabel = html`<div style="position: absolute; top: 12px; right: 24px; font-size: 1rem;
    padding: .1rem .4rem; border: 1px solid currentColor; border-radius: 4px; opacity: .85">${tex`\|u(t)\|`}</div>`;
  // x-axis label, centered below the tick labels
  const xMid = 100 * norms.scale("x").apply(tMax / 2) / size;
  const xLabel = html`<div style="position: absolute; left: ${xMid}%; bottom: 0; transform: translateX(-50%);
    font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1">${tex`t`}</div>`;
  return html`<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: flex-start">
    <div style="flex: 1 1 0; min-width: 260px"><div style="position: relative">${phase}${phaseLabels}</div></div>
    <div style="flex: 1 1 0; min-width: 260px"><div style="position: relative">${norms}${yLabel}${xLabel}</div></div>
  </div>`;
}
```
